Fixes a NaN that the generated Metal code produced on a real Apple GPU, found by this repo's first CI run on macOS.

## Fixed
- `mlp` returned NaN on the Metal GPU: Metal's fast-math `tanh` overflows for |x| > ~44, which the fused GELU reaches. Both GPU backends now clamp the argument to ±10 (no change to any float32 result), and a new `gelu_wide` test graph covers inputs up to ~200 on every backend.
- The Metal GPU step in CI is now blocking: 18/18 zoo programs match NumPy on the macos-latest runner's GPU.

## Downloads
- `kernelforge-0.1.1-py3-none-any.whl`, `kernelforge-0.1.1.tar.gz`: the compiler (pure Python + NumPy).
- `kernelforge-kernels.zip`: the benchmark kernels as source (WGSL with RTX 2060-tuned schedules, MSL with cost-model schedules, C oracle).
- `kf_metal_run-macos-arm64`: the Metal harness binary built on GitHub's macOS runner.

## Not yet verified
- No numbers on an Apple M1: the Metal column of the benchmark table is empty (⏳).
- RTX 2060 numbers were measured on one desktop while other GPU work was running (see README).
